common.proposalNotice: This is a proposal prototype, not an official system adopted by the General Authority of Civil Aviation.

landing.heroTitle: Your self-built drone deserves a legal registration
landing.heroSubtitle: Registration today requires a manufacturer serial number. Self-built and FPV aircraft don't have one, so they stay outside the system. Ajniha replaces the serial number with Remote ID.
landing.gapBody: There is currently no lawful path for a self-built drone operator. No registration, and nowhere sanctioned to fly.
landing.remoteIdTitle: Remote ID instead of a serial number
landing.remoteIdBody: Remote ID is the direction regulation is already moving. Ajniha issues each aircraft a unique identifier that a field inspector can scan.
landing.accountabilityBody: A field inspector scans the code and sees that the aircraft is registered and accountable — without seeing who owns it. Revealing identity is a restricted permission, and every reveal is logged.

rule.title: Registration asks for a serial number
rule.body: Drone registration today rests on a manufacturer's serial number, treated as the airframe's permanent identity.

gap.title: Some aircraft have none
gap.body: A self-built or FPV aircraft is assembled from parts. There is no manufacturer, no serial number, and no field that can honestly be filled in.

consequence.title: So there is nowhere to register, and nowhere to fly
consequence.body: A pilot who cannot register cannot book, and has no sanctioned airspace. The aircraft does not disappear — it flies outside the system.

landing.cardQrAlt: QR code for an example Remote ID card
landing.cardScanHint: Scan it: you reach the same public verification page a field inspector does. This code is reserved for demonstration and belongs to no registered aircraft.
landing.mapBody: The city is restricted by default, with specific permitted areas carved out inside it and absolute no-fly zones layered on top. Flying starts with booking an area, not with take-off.
landing.mapAlt: Diagram of the airspace zones over Riyadh

register.title: Register the aircraft
register.body: Enter the airframe's specifications and photographs. For a self-built drone, the serial number field is not shown at all.

remoteId.title: Receive your Remote ID
remoteId.body: Once approved, your aircraft is issued a Remote ID and a QR code to print and fix to the airframe.

book.title: Book an area and a time
book.body: Choose a permitted area and a slot. The platform checks altitude, weight and operating hours before it approves.

fly.title: Fly within the booking
fly.body: Anyone who scans your aircraft sees a valid registration and an authorised flight — without seeing who you are.

landing.forGacaBody: The oversight side of the same system: decisions on the record, a log with no edit path, and a field verification tool.

queues.title: Review queues
queues.body: Registrations reach a human reviewer who approves, or refuses with a written reason the owner can read.

compliance.title: Compliance indicators
compliance.body: Registration, booking and report volumes, and rejection rates with their reasons.

lookup.title: Field verification
lookup.body: Scanning an aircraft's code returns its registration status at once. Revealing the owner is a restricted power, and every reveal is recorded.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: Every decision and every identity reveal is written to a log the product has no path to edit or delete.

landing.footerLine: Ajniha — a proposed platform for drone registration and airspace booking.

howItWorks.pageLead: From creating an account to taking off — and what a stranger sees when they scan your aircraft. This is the whole path, as a pilot meets it.

account.title: Create your account and complete your profile
account.body: The account is yours, not the aircraft's. You give your name, your contact details and your national ID or Iqama number once, and they carry across every aircraft you register afterwards.
account.detail: A reviewer checks your identity. There is no automated verification and no SMS — a person reads the document and decides.

register.title: Register the aircraft, serial number or not
register.body: You describe the aircraft: build type, weight class, manufacturer and model if it has them, and photographs. The serial number field is optional.
register.detail: This is the entire point. A self-built or FPV aircraft has no serial number, and that does not stop it being registered here.

review.title: A person reviews it
review.body: The registration sits under review until a reviewer opens it, and is then either approved or rejected with a written reason you can read.
review.detail: A rejection is not the end of it: you fix what was asked for and resubmit. Every decision is written to the audit trail under the name of whoever made it.

identity.title: Your Remote ID and QR code are issued
identity.body: On approval the aircraft gets its own Remote ID code, a digital card, and a QR code you can print and fix to the airframe.
identity.detail: The code stays the same for the life of the aircraft, renewal included, so a printed sticker never dies.

book.title: Book a zone and a slot
book.body: You pick a permitted zone and a slot inside its opening hours. The system checks the zone, the ceiling, the weight class, the build type and any temporary closure before it answers.
book.detail: A refusal comes back as specific reasons rather than a generic message, so you know exactly which rule stopped you.

renew.title: Fly, then renew
renew.body: You fly inside the zone you booked and within its window. The registration has a validity period, and you are told before it lapses.
renew.detail: Once it has lapsed the code still scans — it simply reports that the registration has expired instead of that it is valid.

howItWorks.refusalsLead: Everything is closed by default. Better to know that before you drive out to the site.

outside.title: Outside a permitted zone
outside.body: The launch point is inside the Riyadh area but not inside any published permitted zone.

closed.title: Outside opening hours, or during a closure
closed.body: Each zone has two windows a day, and Friday is split around Jumu'ah. A temporary closure overrides the published hours.

ceiling.title: Above the ceiling
ceiling.body: Each zone has a ceiling in metres above ground level. It is not advisory.

capacity.title: The zone is full
capacity.body: Each slot has a limited number of seats. Two bookings for the same place at the same time cannot both succeed.

status.title: The aircraft is not approved
status.body: A draft, a registration still under review, and a revoked or expired one: none of them can book.

howItWorks.privacyLead: Anyone who scans your aircraft sees the registration status, the build type, the weight class and the city of registration. They do not see your name, your mobile number, your ID number, or where you are flying. An authorised reviewer can reveal the owner when they need to — after writing a reason, and the reveal is recorded against their name.
howItWorks.nextBody: Registering here does not need a serial number.

remoteIdPage.pageLead: A digital licence plate for drones: an identifier broadcast during flight that ties what you can see in the sky to a record someone can look up. This page explains the two models the rule rests on — the American one and the Saudi one — and why an Ajniha Remote ID is a workable substitute for a serial number.
remoteIdPage.whatBody: It is not tracking and it is not a camera. It is a short message broadcast from the aircraft while it flies, carrying an identifier, a position, an altitude, a speed and the pilot's location, and any device nearby can receive it.
remoteIdPage.whatBody2: The identifier by itself says nothing about the owner. Its value is that it points at a record: whoever is authorised to look that record up learns who the aircraft belongs to, and everyone else sees a number. That separation between identifier and identity is what makes the model workable at all.
remoteIdPage.faaBody: The FAA's Remote ID rule is Part 89 of Title 14, and it offers three ways to comply.

standard.title: An aircraft that broadcasts by itself
standard.body: An aircraft built to broadcast its own identity.

module.title: A fitted broadcast module
module.body: A part fixed to an aircraft that does not broadcast, which broadcasts on its behalf. This is the route open to home-built aircraft.

fria.title: A recognized area where you may fly without broadcasting
fria.body: A specific site where flight without broadcast is allowed, provided the aircraft stays within visual line of sight.

remoteIdPage.faaIdentityBody: What matters in the rule is that the identity being broadcast is not necessarily the aircraft's serial number. The text offers a choice:
remoteIdPage.faaModuleBody: And with a fitted module, the number broadcast is the module's own serial number, not that of the aircraft carrying it:
remoteIdPage.gacaTitle: The Saudi model: Direct or Network Remote ID
remoteIdPage.gacaBody: Subpart F of GACAR Part 107 carries an explicit application date, and requires every registered aircraft — model aircraft included — to carry one of two systems.
remoteIdPage.gacaDriBody: Direct Remote ID (DRI) broadcasts the operator's registration number and the verification code GACA issued, then the serial number of the fitted add-on:
remoteIdPage.gacaNriBody: Network Remote ID (NRI), by contrast, also requires the aircraft's own serial number — and that is the practical difference between the two routes:
remoteIdPage.gacaVersionNote: The passages above are quoted from Version 4.0 of Part 107, which is the edition that could be obtained. GACA's own log of versions shows the current edition is 5.0, and that its amendments concern standard scenarios and pilot training rather than Subpart F.
remoteIdPage.gapBody: The common belief is that registration requires a manufacturer's serial number. GACA's own documents are more careful than that: the serial is essential information for the Specific Category only, is asked for in the Open Category if it is available, and the identifier an aircraft displays may be the registration certificate number instead.
remoteIdPage.gapBody2: So the gap is not the serial number. It is what the identifier points at: a home-built aircraft has no number and no record tying it to an accountable person, so there is nothing to look up when somebody sees it overhead.
remoteIdPage.gapBody3: From 1 January 2026 this gets sharper still: what has to be broadcast is a registration number issued by an authority, not a factory marking. And whoever issues the number holds the record. That is exactly what Ajniha does.
remoteIdPage.ajnihaBody: A Remote ID issued by the platform, bound to a registered aircraft and to an owner whose identity a person has checked.

code.title: A stable code
code.body: One code for the life of the aircraft, in a form you can read out and say aloud, and it survives renewal.

record.title: A record behind it
record.body: The code points at an approved registration: build type, weight class, city of registration, and an accountable owner.

scan.title: A public page when it is scanned
scan.body: Anyone who scans the code reaches a page stating the registration's status, with nothing about the owner on it.

reveal.title: A reveal that is logged, never automatic
reveal.body: An authorised reviewer can reveal the owner after writing a reason, and the reveal is written to the audit trail before anything is shown.

renewal.title: A sticker that does not die
renewal.body: Renewal does not change the code, because the sticker may have been on the airframe for years.

remoteIdPage.notBody: This is said plainly, because the rest of the page means nothing without it.

notRadio.title: Not a radio
notRadio.body: An Ajniha code is an identifier in a register, not a signal transmitted from the aircraft, and it does not replace a DRI or NRI unit.

notCertified.title: Not a certified system
notCertified.body: The platform has not been evaluated or accepted as a Direct or Network Remote ID system under any regulation.

notGaca.title: Not issued by GACA
notGaca.body: Ajniha is an independent proposal. Nothing here implies that the General Authority of Civil Aviation has approved or adopted it.

notLegal.title: It does not make your flight lawful
notLegal.body: If your aircraft carries a real broadcast module, declare it here for a reviewer to check. The regulation, not this page, remains the authority.

zoneAdmin.title: Zones
zoneAdmin.intro: Draw the airspace and set the rules inside it. Drafts are listed first and are invisible to pilots.
zoneAdmin.newZoneHint: Saved as a draft — nobody sees it until it is published.
zoneAdmin.newZoneIntro: Draw the boundary on the map, then set the rules that apply inside it.
zoneAdmin.noCities: There are no cities yet, and a zone belongs to one. Adding cities comes later in this feature.
zoneAdmin.geometryNone: Nothing drawn yet. Pick a drawing tool and trace the zone on the map.
zoneAdmin.rulesIntro: Every rule here is read by the airspace engine on each booking request. Under each field is what it does to pilots.
zoneAdmin.codeHint: A code somebody reads over a radio, like RUH-P-01. Latin letters, digits and hyphens.
zoneAdmin.cityHint: The city this zone sits in.

kindHint.permitted: Flying is allowed here, within this zone's rules.
kindHint.restricted: Flying is refused unless a permitted zone is carved out inside it.
kindHint.no_fly: Every flight is refused, and this beats any permitted zone it overlaps.

zoneAdmin.authorityRefHint: The decision or reference this zone rests on, if there is one.
zoneAdmin.ceilingHint: The highest altitude allowed inside. Leave empty if the zone has no ceiling of its own.
zoneAdmin.floorHint: The lowest altitude allowed. A flight planned below it is refused.
zoneAdmin.capacityHint: How many aircraft may hold the same slot. The last seat closes the slot to everyone else.
zoneAdmin.slotDurationHint: The booking grid. A slot longer than the opening hours produces no bookable slot at all.
zoneAdmin.minLeadHint: How long before a slot starts booking closes. Zero means bookable up to take-off.
zoneAdmin.maxAdvanceHint: How far ahead a pilot may book.
zoneAdmin.slotsPerDay: Maximum slots per pilot per day
zoneAdmin.slotsPerDayHint: Stops one pilot booking out a whole day in a zone with few seats.
zoneAdmin.maxWeightClassHint: Heavier aircraft are refused. Leave unlimited if weight makes no difference here.
zoneAdmin.permittedBuildTypesHint: Unticking self-built and FPV makes this a commercial-only zone — and those pilots are who this system exists for. An empty list is refused: a zone nobody may fly in is a no-fly zone.
zoneAdmin.autoApproveHint: Bookings are approved immediately with no human reviewer, unless the pilot has a recent no-show record.
zoneAdmin.nightAllowedHint: Without it, every slot before sunrise or after sunset is refused even while the zone is open.
zoneAdmin.requiresBroadcastRidHint: Excludes every pilot without a verified broadcast module — verified by a reviewer, not merely declared. Check what that costs before switching it on.
zoneAdmin.draftNotice: Saving does not publish the zone. It stays invisible to pilots.

tool.hint: Click to add a point, and click the first point to close the shape. Then Edit points to drag one, delete one, or add one at the midpoint of an edge. A new boundary snaps to the points of neighbouring zones.

problems.code_invalid: A zone code is Latin letters, digits and hyphens, like RUH-P-01.
problems.code_taken: Another zone already uses that code.
problems.city_required: Choose the city this zone sits in.
problems.kind_invalid: That zone kind does not exist.
problems.name_too_long: That name is longer than the field holds.
problems.notes_too_long: Those notes are longer than the field holds.
problems.ceiling_invalid: The ceiling must be a whole number between 1 and 1000 metres, or empty.
problems.floor_invalid: The floor must be a whole number and not negative.
problems.floor_above_ceiling: The floor must be below the ceiling.
problems.capacity_invalid: Seats per slot must be between 1 and 50.
problems.slot_duration_invalid: A slot must be between 15 minutes and 8 hours.
problems.lead_invalid: That lead time is not valid.
problems.advance_invalid: The advance window must be between one day and a year.
problems.slots_per_day_invalid: That number of slots per pilot per day is not valid.
problems.weight_class_invalid: That weight class does not exist.
problems.build_types_invalid: That build type does not exist.
problems.build_types_empty: Choose at least one build type. A zone nobody may fly in is a no-fly zone.
problems.geometry_unsupported_type: A boundary has to be a polygon.
problems.geometry_ring_too_short: A boundary needs at least three points.
problems.geometry_position_not_a_pair: One of the points is not a coordinate pair.
problems.geometry_position_not_finite: One of the points carries a value that is not a number.
problems.geometry_self_intersecting: The boundary crosses itself. A self-intersecting polygon makes “is this point inside the zone” meaningless, so redraw the crossing part.
problems.geometry_too_many_vertices: {count} points, over the limit of {max}. Simplify the boundary.
problems.geometry_outside_saudi_arabia: The boundary falls outside Saudi Arabia. Check the coordinate order — longitude first, then latitude.
problems.geometry_area_too_small: Only {areaSqM} square metres, against a minimum of {minSqM}. That is a mis-click, not a zone.
problems.geometry_ring_auto_closed: The boundary was closed for you: its last point did not return to the first.
problems.geometry_winding_corrected: The boundary's drawing direction was corrected to match the GeoJSON standard. A hole must run opposite to its outer ring, or it renders as an island rather than a gap.
problems.not_found: That zone could not be found.
problems.not_authenticated: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
problems.hour_weekday_invalid: That is not a day of the week.
problems.hour_not_ordered: The closing time must be after the opening one. A window never crosses midnight — split it into two.
problems.hour_overlap: Two windows overlap on the same day. An overlap gives one hour two slot grids and two seats where there is one.
problems.hour_too_many_per_day: Too many windows on one day.
problems.publish_geometry_invalid: The drawn boundary is not valid.
problems.publish_name_missing: Both the Arabic and English names are required before publishing.
problems.publish_hours_missing: A permitted zone needs at least one operating window, or it publishes and derives no slots at all.
problems.publish_capacity_invalid: Capacity must be at least one.
problems.publish_overlaps_no_fly: The boundary overlaps a published no-fly zone ({zones}). Booking asks the engine about a zone rather than a point, so it cannot see this overlap — the map can. Move the boundary before publishing.
problems.archive_has_bookings: Archiving is refused while a future booking stands. Suspend the zone first — that cancels them and tells each pilot why.
problems.geometry_impact_unconfirmed: Moving a published zone's boundary needs confirmation once you have seen the bookings it affects.
problems.invalid_transition: That change is not allowed from the current status.
problems.already_applied: The zone is already in that status.
problems.reason_required: Write a reason in both languages, at least twenty characters each.
problems.closure_start_required: Choose the date and time the closure starts.
problems.closure_end_required: Choose the date and time the closure ends.
problems.closure_not_ordered: The closure must end after it starts.
problems.closure_already_over: That window has already passed. A closure that has ended cancels nothing.
problems.closure_too_long: A closure longer than ninety days is not temporary. Suspend the zone instead — that is reversible and tells every pilot why.
problems.closure_reason_ar_required: The Arabic reason is required, at least {min} characters.
problems.closure_reason_en_required: The English reason is required, at least {min} characters.
problems.closure_reason_too_long: That reason is longer than the field holds.
problems.closure_authority_ref_too_long: That reference is longer than the field holds.
problems.zone_not_publishable: Only a published or suspended zone can be closed.
problems.closure_published: A published closure cannot be deleted. It has already cancelled flights and told those pilots why, and removing the row would reopen the airspace while leaving all of that standing.

zoneAdmin.hoursIntro: The week starts on Sunday. Times are Riyadh local, and a window opens and closes on the same day — it never crosses midnight. Friday usually takes two windows, around Jumu'ah.
zoneAdmin.hoursUnsaved: The hours on screen have not been saved yet.
zoneAdmin.previewIntro: The slots these hours derive, by the same calculation a pilot sees. Slots are never stored — these are the slots themselves, not an estimate of them.
zoneAdmin.previewNone: These hours derive no slots on this day. The window is shorter than the slot length ({duration} minutes), or there is no window at all.
zoneAdmin.previewNightNotice: Night flight is not allowed in this zone, and the marked slots fall before sunrise ({sunrise}) or after sunset ({sunset}) — the engine refuses them however the zone is opened.
zoneAdmin.previewUnsavedNotice: The preview uses the hours on screen, including any you have not saved.
zoneAdmin.lifecycleIntro: A draft is invisible to pilots and produces no slots. Publishing is the moment a drawing becomes airspace.
zoneAdmin.publishReady: This zone is ready to publish.
zoneAdmin.suspendIntro: Suspending withdraws the airspace and cancels every booking still ahead in it. The reason reaches each pilot in their language, quoted as written.
zoneAdmin.archiveIntro: Archiving is final and cancels nothing. It is refused while any future booking stands — suspend the zone first.
zoneAdmin.impactNone: No future bookings in this zone.
zoneAdmin.impactCount: {n, plural, one {One future booking} other {{count} future bookings}}
zoneAdmin.geometryImpactHeading: What this boundary change would do
zoneAdmin.geometryImpactIntro: The new boundary does not contain the old one — it was cut back or moved. The flights below go back to review. They are not cancelled, and each keeps its seat.
zoneAdmin.geometryImpactNoLaunchPoint: A booking names a zone and carries no launch point, so nothing can say which flight in particular was in the part you removed. Every approved flight still ahead is therefore shown, and a person decides.
zoneAdmin.geometryImpactConfirm: Save and send these back to review
zoneAdmin.geometryImpactNone: The new boundary contains the old one, so no booking is affected.
zoneAdmin.geometryPublishedNotice: This zone is published. Moving its boundary shows you the effect on future bookings before you save.
zoneAdmin.statusDraftNotice: Draft: invisible to pilots, and it produces no slots.
zoneAdmin.statusSuspendedNotice: Suspended: unbookable, and the bookings ahead of it were cancelled.
zoneAdmin.previewUnavailable: The preview waits until the hours are valid — fix what is reported above first.
zoneAdmin.statusActiveNotice: Published: visible to pilots, and deriving bookable slots.
zoneAdmin.fanOutFailed: The zone is suspended, but the job that cancels its bookings could not be queued. The pilots have not been told and their bookings still stand — check that Inngest is running, then try again.
zoneAdmin.closuresIntro: A closure is a window over this zone. While a published one stands every flight inside it is refused, and publishing it cancels every booking the window covers.
zoneAdmin.closureNewIntro: Saved unpublished. Nothing is refused and nobody is cancelled until you publish it.
zoneAdmin.closureTimeHint: Riyadh local time, typed as 24-hour HH:mm — 18:00, not 6 PM. A closure may run across midnight and across days.
zoneAdmin.closureReasonHint: Quoted verbatim to every pilot whose flight this cancels, in their own language. Both are required, at least {min} characters each.
zoneAdmin.closureAuthorityRefHint: The notice or decision this closure rests on, if there is one.
zoneAdmin.closureCheck: Show the flights inside this window
zoneAdmin.closureCreateHint: Saving does not publish it. The flights it would cancel are listed again before you do.
zoneAdmin.closurePreviewNone: No bookings fall inside this window.
zoneAdmin.closureOverlapsNotice: Another closure on this zone already covers part of this window. Publishing this one refuses nothing new there, and the flights that window covered have already been cancelled.
zoneAdmin.closurePublishIntro: Publishing puts the closure into force immediately and cancels the flights below. Each pilot is notified and emailed with the reason as written. It cannot be undone from here.
zoneAdmin.closureCancelCount: {n, plural, one {One flight will be cancelled} other {{count} flights will be cancelled}}
zoneAdmin.closureFanOutFailed: The closure is published and the airspace is already closed, but the cancellations could not be queued — the background job service is not reachable. The pilots holding these slots have not been told yet.
zoneAdmin.closureZoneNotCloseable: Only a published or suspended zone can be closed. A draft is invisible to pilots and an archived zone no longer exists, so a closure over either would refuse nothing.

cityAdmin.title: Cities
cityAdmin.intro: A zone belongs to a city, so this list is what decides where anything can be drawn at all.
cityAdmin.modelledHint: A city is marked modelled when this build carries authored airspace for it. Only Riyadh does, and the Riyadh zones are authored for this proposal — they are not official GACA airspace.
cityAdmin.newIntro: The centre is where a map opens over the city. It is not a boundary.
cityAdmin.centroidHint: Decimal degrees, WGS84. Riyadh is latitude 24.7136, longitude 46.6753 — a latitude above 33 usually means the two are the wrong way round.

problems.city_code_invalid: A city code is three uppercase Latin letters, like RUH.
problems.city_code_taken: Another city already uses that code.
problems.city_name_too_long: That name is longer than the field holds.
problems.city_centroid_required: Enter the latitude and the longitude as numbers.
problems.city_centroid_outside_saudi_arabia: That centre falls outside Saudi Arabia. Check the order — latitude first, then longitude.
problems.not_authenticated: Your session has ended. Sign in again.

analytics.title: Analytics and compliance
analytics.intro: What is actually happening across the platform. Every number here is derived from a live query.
analytics.tilesFixedNote: The tiles above describe the state now and do not follow the selected period; median review turnaround is fixed to the last 30 days. The period changes the charts only.
analytics.rtlNote: The time axis on every chart runs left to right in both languages — reversing it for Arabic misleads more than it accommodates. Labels and tooltips are Arabic; numerals stay Latin and dates are Gregorian. The one exception is bookings by zone, whose axis is a count rather than a time.
analytics.tileExpiringHint: Active registrations nearing the end of their validity
analytics.tableToggle: Show the numbers as a table
analytics.registrationsNote: Self-built and FPV aircraft carry no manufacturer serial number, and could not have been registered at all under a scheme that requires one.
analytics.registrationsShare: {share} of the registrations issued in this period ({count} of {total}) are aircraft with no manufacturer serial number — they could not have been registered under a scheme that requires one.
analytics.registrationsEmpty: No registrations were issued in this period.
analytics.outcomesNote: Read from the audit trail as each decision was made, not from the aircraft's status today.
analytics.outcomesEmpty: No review decisions were made in this period.
analytics.turnaroundNote: A median hides the long tail, and the tail is what a regulator answers for.
analytics.turnaroundEmpty: No review decisions were made in this period.
analytics.zonesNote: The top eight zones. The export carries every zone.
analytics.zonesEmpty: No zone was booked in this period.
analytics.utilisationTitle: Zone utilisation by day and hour
analytics.utilisationNote: The week starts on Sunday and hours are Riyadh time. Pending requests are not counted — this measures authorised flights, not demand.
analytics.utilisationEmpty: No flights were authorised in this period.
analytics.noShowNote: Concluded flights only: attended and not attended. A booking cancelled in advance is not a compliance failure.
analytics.noShowEmpty: No flight concluded in this period.
analytics.resolutionsNote: Who read the code: the public, or the enforcement side. A code nobody reads is a sticker.
analytics.resolutionsEmpty: No Remote ID was resolved in this period.

audit.appendOnly: This log is append-only. Nothing in the platform edits or deletes a row of it — there is no control, and no server action.
audit.browsingNotAudited: Browsing this log is not itself audited. Revealing a pilot's identity and looking up a Remote ID always are, and appear here.
audit.diffEmpty: This event recorded no field-level change.
audit.empty: There are no events in the log yet.
audit.exportNote: Exporting the log is itself written to the log.
audit.geometryNote: The old boundary is dashed, the new one solid. These zones are authored for this proposal and are not official GACA airspace.
audit.geometryUnavailable: The map cannot be drawn for this event.
audit.intro: Everything that has happened on the platform, newest first: who did what, in what role, and why.
audit.pageNote: Paging follows each event's timestamp and id, so no row is repeated or skipped when new events arrive mid-scroll.
audit.title: Audit log
